generation.mode: single built-in ImageGen edit with edit-target as Image 1 and style canon as reference-only Image 2

lightingIsotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient magnitude peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; water and its four immediate neighbours are excluded, as are gradients below 12 luminance units.
lightingIsotropy.visualCheck: No whole-cell sun gradient or cast-shadow field is obvious, but basalt repeatedly has pale upper facets and darker side faces, and conifers retain light-dark form modelling. The aggregate statistic does not establish the literal equal-value rule.

buildableVsSteepFraction.basis: Manual estimated fraction of non-water land area at native source resolution.
buildableVsSteepFraction.method: Broad coherent pale plateau benches count as buildable; the immediate broken shore rim and short exposed column faces count as steep; talus, shingle, scattered boulders, scrub, and conifer groups make up the remainder. Approximate uncertainty is plus or minus 0.08 per fraction.

landDepthFromSouthEdge.method: For each source column, measure from the south edge to the deepest connected masked sea pixel and convert source pixels across the 97.6 m cell extent.

edgeTopology.authorityConflict: The hard topology rule requires sea on the complete east and west edges, but the supplied edit target already contains neighbour-authored land on those edge segments and separately requires painted neighbour pixels to remain in place. The preserve-neighbour-paint rule governed the edit; the resulting topology failure is reported rather than silently repainting authoritative context.

crown.method: Manual outer-foliage-width census of every visually distinguishable conifer, including saplings, overlapping crowns, and edge-clipped crowns; native median 31 px scaled by 2560/1254 and converted at 4.8 cm per final pixel.

waterMask.encoding: Opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha.
waterMask.method: Flooded edge-connected source-raster teal and blue, grew through adjacent source-painted pale surf and wash, filled only classifier pinholes, retained the largest connected coastal component, and preserved visible dry shoreline rock, stacks, and skerries as terrain.
waterMask.visualInspection: Native overlay inspection found open sea, shoreline surf, wash between shore rocks, reflections, and ripple highlights included; source-visible dry columns, stacks, skerries, and talus remain outside the mask.

refusalReasons: The plateau continuation is too deep: 40.47-62.11 m with a 49.34 m median, while the hard requirement is 15-40 m and never more.

Land reaches both east and west edges. Those pixels are already present in the supplied neighbour paint and were preserved under the edit-target authority, but the delivered cell still fails the stated all-sea side-edge topology.
Repeated pale basalt caps over darker side faces and modelled conifer sides violate the literal neutral-lighting rule.
The central shoreline exposes substantial viewer-facing column sides instead of reducing the north shore to ground ending at a thin broken rim seen from behind.
Several column runs remain similarly sized, upright, and clean-capped rather than consistently broken, split, leaning, and weathered.
openRisks: The water mask is mechanically complete against the source, but it faithfully preserves the source candidate's noncompliant land extent and side-edge topology.
Buildable and steep fractions and the crown census are manual image measurements rather than surveyed geometry.
No second ImageGen call was made because the returned source was square and the task authorizes a retry only for non-square framing.
Seam continuity and overall visual quality remain director and owner judgments; this report makes no visual acceptance claim.
